research_text:
# Research brief: javax.crypto.spec.GCMParameterSpec

**Source limits up front.** Question 4 could not be answered from the CrySL source. My search tool never returned the text of `GCMParameterSpec.crysl`, and I had no direct fetch. Questions 1–3 rely on the Oracle Javadoc, the JCA reference guide and NIST, but I only saw search-result excerpts of those pages, not the full pages.

## Q1. What the class governs, and what the finding refers to

- **What it governs.** <https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/GCMParameterSpec.html> says the class specifies the parameters a `Cipher` needs in Galois/Counter Mode. Those parameters are the IV and `tLen`, the authentication tag length in bits.
- **Constructors.** There are two:
  - `GCMParameterSpec(int tLen, byte[] src)` takes the whole buffer as the IV.
  - `GCMParameterSpec(int tLen, byte[] src, int offset, int len)` takes `len` bytes of `src` starting at `offset` as the IV.
- **Copying.** The Java SE 8 Javadoc says the buffer contents are copied to protect against later modification (<https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/javax/crypto/spec/GCMParameterSpec.html>).
- **What the finding refers to.** The finding concerns the IV byte array (`src`, or the `offset`/`len` slice of it) passed to one of these constructors.
  - The finding text says the IV "was not observed to come from a randomized source".
  - The Javadoc does not mention randomness or provenance, so that wording comes from the detector rule, not from the API documentation.
- **What the spec does not cover.** The class only holds values. Key and IV reuse across operations is governed by `Cipher` (see Q2).

## Q2. Documented correct usage and remediation

- **Tag length.** The Javadoc (JDK 17 link above) says the GCM specification allows `tLen` of only {128, 120, 112, 104, 96}, or {64, 32} for certain applications. It adds that other values can be specified but not all providers will support them.
- **Constructor input errors.**
  - Both constructors throw `IllegalArgumentException` if `tLen` is negative or `src` is null.
  - The four-argument form also throws it if `len` or `offset` is negative, or if `offset + len` exceeds the array length (Java SE 8 Javadoc above).
  - The Javadoc does not say `len == 0` is rejected. That is my reading of the excerpt, not an explicit statement.
- **Key and IV reuse (JCA Reference Guide).** <https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/20/security/java-cryptography-architecture-jca-reference-guide.html> says callers should not re-use key and IV combinations for encryption. Its sample code includes a comment that the IV must change if the same key is used for encryption again.
- **Cipher reuse (`Cipher` Javadoc).** <https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/Cipher.html> says that after each GCM encryption, callers should re-initialize the `Cipher` with GCM parameters that have a different IV. The Java SE 8 version (<https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/javax/crypto/Cipher.html>) says repeated IVs expose GCM encryption to forgery attacks.
- **Randomness.** I found no Oracle statement that the IV must be random, so the Javadoc gives no "use a random IV" instruction.
  - NIST SP 800-38D (<https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/legacy/sp/nistspecialpublication800-38d.pdf>) requires IVs to be unique per key (Sec. 8). It defines a deterministic construction (8.2.1) and an RBG-based construction (8.2.2).
  - Random generation is therefore one allowed way to meet uniqueness, not the only one.
  - This supports the supplied false-positive shape about deterministic IVs.
- **Recommended remediation.** The documented remedy for IV reuse is to supply a fresh, unique IV and re-initialize the cipher. No source I found documents "replace the transformation" as a fix.
  - The policy rule "a transformation-only replacement is insufficient when an initialized Cipher or nonce is reused" is consistent with the Cipher Javadoc.
  - The policy rule "never introduce a constant key, IV or nonce" is consistent with the uniqueness requirement.
- **Reuse enforcement is not uniform.** The OpenJDK review thread for JDK-8349946 (<https://www.mail-archive.com/security-dev@openjdk.org/msg15578.html>) proposes `Cipher` Javadoc changes. The wording there is draft review text, not final documentation. The reuse guard behaviour is also discussed in <https://github.com/tink-crypto/tink/issues/208>, which is a community source and not authoritative.

## Q3. Compatibility

- **Platform support.**
  - The class has been available since Java 1.7 (`@since 1.7` in <https://github.com/openjdk-mirror/jdk7u-jdk/blob/master/src/share/classes/javax/crypto/spec/GCMParameterSpec.java>).
  - On Android it was added in API level 19 (<https://developer.android.com/reference/javax/crypto/spec/GCMParameterSpec>).
  - The JDK 17 Javadoc says that not every provider supports every `tLen`.
- **Persisted and wire formats.**
  - `GCMParameterSpec` has no serialized or wire format of its own. I found no Javadoc statement about persisted formats.
  - Separately, the SunJCE `AlgorithmParameters` "GCM" implementation encodes parameters in the RFC 5084 ASN.1 `GCMParameters` structure (<https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5084.txt>; JDK source <https://github.com/openjdk/jdk13/blob/master/src/java.base/share/classes/sun/security/util/GCMParameters.java>).
  - In that RFC the tag length (`aes-ICVlen`) defaults to 12 and is limited to 12–16 bytes. The nonce is the GCM IV.
  - Whether application code relies on that encoding, or on its own framing such as an IV prefix, is a repository question that I did not examine.
- **Decryption.** The JCA guide says the same AAD and GCM parameters must be supplied to decrypt.
  - Any change to the IV scheme or tag length must stay readable for previously stored or transmitted ciphertext.
  - Decrypt-side IVs come from the data and are not generated.
- **Migration path.** I found no official migration guidance. The `GCMParameterSpec` Javadoc has no deprecation notice in the versions I saw (7, 8, 9, 11, 17, 25, 26).

## Q4. The CrySL rule text (not verifiable by me)

The rule URL is <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/refs/heads/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/GCMParameterSpec.crysl>. I could not retrieve or quote it, so I cannot give a verbatim matching clause. I also cannot say which method names and receiver types the rule matches. I cannot say whether it constrains the parameter list, or what condition it then evaluates. Nor can I say whether it could match a method that only shares a name with the governed API.

- **The supplied `research_input`.** It describes events c1 and c2, `ORDER Con`, and the predicates `randomized[src]` and `preparedGCM[this]`. I did not verify any of this, and it is untrusted data.
- **Papers on CrySL in general.** The CrySL papers (<https://bodden.de/pubs/ksa+18crysl.pdf>, <https://www.bodden.de/pubs/tse19CrySL.pdf>) name `GCMParameterSpec` as an example of a rule without parameter constraints in the version they evaluated. That version may not match the current file, so it does not settle the question.
- **Related rule files.** The repository directory is <https://github.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/tree/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture>. The `Cipher.crysl` rule is at <https://github.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/blob/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/Cipher.crysl>. Neither was opened.

## Unresolved

1. The exact text of `GCMParameterSpec.crysl`, including its event patterns, constraints and predicate definitions.
2. How the detector's analysis defines or evaluates "randomized" provenance.
3. Any official Oracle statement requiring a random IV, as opposed to a unique one.
4. Any official migration guidance for existing stored or transmitted GCM data.
